findings.title: The repeated operator and divergent courses

findings.containment: The HFT trace itself presents a live alternative of one-time eschatological preparation rather than present path-dependence. findings.title: Actions train affordances

Repeated enactment therefore supplies the trigger that changes facilitation from an after-the-fact assignment into a course shaped by what has been practiced.
findings.reader_payoff: The verse's future preparation becomes newly legible as an accumulated consequence of posture: the difficult route is not merely announced, it is shown as the route that a prior pattern has made easier to continue.

findings.title: Hoarded means become straitened
findings.claim: Within the supplied sequence, the hard destination can also be read as the material reversal of hoarded sufficiency: withholding and claimed independence seek to preserve means, then wealth is shown unable to suffice at the fall, so what was kept as protection becomes incapacity.
findings.mechanism: The focus's hardship endpoint and the attributed abundance facet contact the 92:8 withholding and self-sufficiency posture, then the 92:11 wealth and fall contacts expose the failure of that security strategy. The sequence changes hardship from an unspecified punishment into the narrowing of means that the prior posture tried to prevent.
findings.reader_payoff: The hard route gains a concrete economic contour: the resource hoarded as protection is carried forward to the moment when it cannot perform its protective work.
findings.containment: The HFT record preserves a live alternative in which wealth fails only in an eschatological scene and no socioeconomic process is implied. That conversion of security into incapacity is therefore retained as a qualified attributed inference, not as the sole explanation of the endpoint.

epistemic.reason: The HFT record has complete supplied anchors and a focus return, but its context roots and roles are legacy-unbound and its hoarding-to-incapacity arrow is explicitly inferred.
